docs.title: Welcome!
docs.text: Thank you for coming to this site. I hope it can prove a valuable resource for help with any issues you may face with my software.

docs.title: What is this about?
docs.text: This is the home of the documentation for all plugins and other tools as developed by Paladinleeds. If you wish to figure out how to receive help, check out the Support Portal page.

docs.title: So what stuff am I making?
docs.text: More details to be announced on that front.

docs.title: What happened to StreamSharp?
docs.text: This is no longer being developed on my personal account and is being instead developed through an org account, so their documentation page will cover it instead. This is due to the aim to have multiple maintainers for StreamSharp, whereas my plugins will only have a singular maintainer for the official version.

docs.title: Support Portal
docs.text: If you're having trouble with a plugin, there are 2 stages in the "self-service" part of support, these are as follows:

docs.title: 1. Checking the help pages
docs.text: Every piece of software will have its own (set of) page(s) of information surrounding it. In the first instance you should check these pages and see if it solves your issue. FAQs will be included on these pages in order to help save time.

docs.title: 2. Accessing Discord
docs.text: If you cannot find your answer on our help pages, then you will need to join our Discord here. Once you join the server, state in the onboarding process that you wish to receive technical support. This will give you access to the help channels.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text: This is for full applications that don't fall under any other category. I will provide more information about this at a later date.

docs.title: Android Applications
docs.text: I am working on Android applications as well as my macro keyboard plugins. Any Android apps I make for Android will be talked about here. However this is for Android apps that don't fit into another category.

docs.title: Apple Applications
docs.text: There is currently an application under development for the Apple ecosystem. More information about this will be provided as it becomes available. However, this application is expected to become multiplatform after an initial Apple-only run.

docs.title: Multiplatform Applications
docs.text: I am working on some multiplatform applications alongside my other projects. Any products I develop under this category will be mentioned here, provided they don't fall under any other category.

docs.title: Plugin Hub
docs.text: Please note that any officially supported manufacturers will have their own set of plugins listed along the sidebar. Currently, only Elgato devices are being developed for.

docs.title: Plugin master list
docs.text:
Here you will find a list of various plugins that I have produced. You will be able to use the sidebar to select the plugin you want more information about. I hope this helps.

These are separated into two categories: Computer and iPad.

docs.title: Plugins for use on computers
docs.text: In here you will find the list of plugins made for use on computers. Primarily those running Windows and Mac, though Linux ports may exist for some of the plugins.

docs.title: Compatibility Overview
docs.text:
I strive to make my plugins functional on multiple operating systems, along with multiple device types. However, I am unable to check every single device. Thus, I allow users to submit claims to state whether or not plugins are working.

Support ranking

Support will be ranked in the following way:

  1. - Fully working, tested by developer
  2. - Claim: Fully working, tested by community
  3. - Partially working, tested by developer
  4. - Claim: Partially working, tested by community
  5. - Not working at all, tested by developer
  6. - Claim: Not working at all, tested by community
  7. - Will not work on specific device model (due to limitations on the device)
  8. - Untested

This will be placed in information for individual plugin functionality, allowing you to see how this functionality is compatible on a per-action basis. Notes may also be provided dependent on the ranking.

Support checks

We check plugins under functionality types rather than against specific devices. Here are the functionality types available:

  • Dial
  • Key
  • Touch
  • Panel (think the InfoBar on the Stream Deck Neo)
Information regarding profiles

When specific profiles are brought into play for plugins, these will then have compatibility checks against specific Stream Deck hardware. These will be tested as follows.

  • 15 (both Mk1 and Mk2)
  • XL
  • Mini
  • Plus
  • Pedal
  • Neo
  • Studio
A warning regarding Stream Deck Mobile

Due to the new Stream Deck mobile setup, it is difficult to test this, as there are now large fluctuations in the sizing available. The reason for this is the new app allows you to configure your board to have anywhere from one to eight rows, and the same applies to columns (and these settings are completely independent of each other).

As a compromise, we will list the minimum amount of rows and columns required for the profile to be considered usable, or we will state if it just outright will not work

docs.title: Unsupported hardware
docs.text:
I am also aware of devices that utilise Stream Deck plugins but do not directly interface with the Elgato Stream Deck software. I will not be testing these devices, and users who submit compatibility check information about these devices will have their submissions refused.

Danger

These devices that don't interface directly with the Stream Deck software are using reverse-engineering and other hacks to gain functionality. As a result, they often have quirks that cause issues within plugins, and these quirks often have no rhyme or reason to them. Consequently, support will not be provided if there are issues (it is impossible for us to provide support for these unofficial devices). You would have to liaise with other users outside of the server.

Notice regarding adding support

Submissions to support these devices that interface with Stream Deck plugins while not using the Elgato software will not be considered. I will only support official devices.

If a plugin is open source, it will be AGPL licenced. This means you will be allowed to modify the code to make it work for your own devices, however you must also licence it under that same AGPL licence (and as such comply with the terms), and you must use a different plugin name (as this is a trademark issue, and it must be something that an average individual will not reasonably confuse with the original product name).

Anyone using your version of this plugin may not access support from my support portals, so please ensure you have your own support available. You will not receive support from my support portals in terms of being able to modify the code to function with these unofficial devices.
